set_title: Gait signs: Romberg sign, Steppage gait, Magnetic gait, Festinating gait, Wide-based ataxic gait and Circumduction gait
stem: A 38-year-old strict vegan has numb feet and impaired vibration sense. He stands steadily with his feet together and eyes open, but sways and falls when he closes his eyes.
oneliner: 38M vegan, numb feet + steady eyes open, falls when eyes close → ?

whyNot.A: Steppage is a walking pattern; his finding occurs **standing with eyes closed**
whyNot.C: Magnetic gait is hesitant walking; he **falls only when his eyes close**
whyNot.D: Festinating gait is shuffling with quickening steps; his sway occurs **only with eyes closed**
whyNot.E: Cerebellar ataxia sways with **eyes open** as well

why: Falling only when the **eyes close** is a positive Romberg sign: proprioception from the dorsal columns is lost, as in B12 deficiency.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Falls when eyes close, stable when open
Foot drop, common fibular (peroneal) nerve injury
Short shuffling steps that speed up
Broad stance, staggering, can't tandem walk
Stiff leg swung out in an arc

idea.rule: Falls with eyes closed only = dorsal column (position sense) loss.

set_title: Heat and cold triggered signs: Uhthoff phenomenon, Raynaud phenomenon, Ice pack test, Cold-induced acrocyanosis and Ice cube test
stem: A 24-year-old man has fever and cough from Mycoplasma pneumonia. Two weeks later his ears, nose and fingertips turn blue in cold weather and normalize with warming. Hemoglobin is 8 g/dL with raised indirect bilirubin. Direct Coombs test is positive for complement only, and the smear shows red cell clumping.
oneliner: 24M, 2 wk after Mycoplasma + blue ears and fingers in the cold, hemolysis, clumping → antibody?
ask: Which antibody best explains this sign?

options.D: Donath-Landsteiner IgG against the P antigen
options.E: IgM against the red cell I antigen

whyNot.A: Warm IgG gives hemolysis without cold blueness; his **complement-only Coombs and cold symptoms** differ
whyNot.B: That causes ITP with bleeding; he has **hemolysis and red cell clumping**
whyNot.C: Anti-centromere antibodies mark limited scleroderma; he has **post-Mycoplasma hemolysis**
whyNot.D: That causes paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria after viral illness; his **smear shows clumping, Coombs complement-only**

answer: IgM against the red cell I antigen
why: Cold agglutinin IgM binds red cells in cooler peripheral sites and fixes complement. **Post-Mycoplasma** onset, clumping and complement-only Coombs are classic.

idea.rule: Blue ears and fingers in cold + hemolysis + Mycoplasma/EBV = cold agglutinin IgM.
also: Treat by avoiding cold; rituximab if severe

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Heat or exercise worsens neurologic symptoms
Fingers white, blue, then red with cold
Blue fingertips and ears in cold
Ice on skin raises a wheal

set_title: Nail signs: Clubbing, Koilonychia, Beau lines, Mees lines, Nail pitting and Terry nails
stem: A 34-year-old woman has had 8 months of fatigue, heavy menses and a craving for ice. Her nails are thin and brittle with depressed centers and raised edges, so that a drop of water would rest on them. Hemoglobin is 9.2 g/dL and MCV is 72 fL.
oneliner: 34F, heavy menses + ice craving + thin nails with raised edges → ?

whyNot.A: Clubbing has bulbous tips and lost angle; her nails are **concave and thin**
whyNot.B: Beau lines are transverse grooves; her nails are **uniformly concave**
whyNot.D: Terry nails are white with a red band; hers are **concave**
whyNot.E: Pitting is small punched-out pits; her nails are **concave and thin**

why: Thin, concave, spoon-shaped nails are koilonychia, classically from iron deficiency anemia. **Heavy menses, ice craving and microcytosis** support it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Loss of nail fold angle, bulbous tips
Nail growth arrest: chemotherapy, severe illness
Small punched-out pits in nail plate
White nail with thin distal red band

idea.rule: Spoon-shaped nails + microcytic anemia = koilonychia = iron deficiency.
also: Pica, such as ice craving, is typical
Low ferritin and high TIBC confirm

set_title: Eye findings in syndromes: Brushfield spots, Upward lens dislocation, Downward lens dislocation, Blue sclerae and Leukocoria
stem: The parents of a 14-month-old boy notice that in flash photographs his right pupil looks white while the left looks red. He tracks poorly with the right eye.
oneliner: 14-month-old, flash photo shows white right pupil, poor tracking → ?

whyNot.A: Brushfield spots are iris speckles; his **pupil reflex is white**
whyNot.C: Upward lens dislocation leaves the red reflex; his **pupil looks white**
whyNot.D: Downward lens dislocation is a lens position change; his **pupillary reflex is white**
whyNot.E: Blue sclerae tint the scleral surface; his **pupil appears white**

why: A white pupillary reflex is leukocoria. In a child it demands exclusion of retinoblastoma (RB1 loss); congenital cataract and other causes also occur.

idea.rule: White pupillary reflex in a child = leukocoria; rule out retinoblastoma.
also: Also from cataract or retinal detachment

set_title: Nutrition deficiency signs: Bitot spots, Corkscrew hairs, Casal necklace, Rachitic rosary and Flaky paint dermatosis
stem: A 72-year-old man who lives alone and eats mostly canned meat and white bread has had bleeding gums and bruising for a month. His legs show purpura around follicles, with bent, coiled shafts emerging from them.
oneliner: 72M, poor diet + bleeding gums + perifollicular purpura, coiled shafts → ?

whyNot.A: Bitot spots are conjunctival; his findings are **perifollicular purpura**
whyNot.C: Casal necklace is a photosensitive neck rash; he has **bleeding gums**
whyNot.D: Rachitic rosary is rib beading in children; he is **72 with bleeding gums**
whyNot.E: Flaky paint dermatosis has edema and peeling skin, not **bleeding gums and purpura**

why: Coiled hair shafts with **perifollicular purpura and bleeding gums** are corkscrew hairs; vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen hydroxylation of proline and lysine.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Peeling patches with edema and big belly

idea.rule: Perifollicular hemorrhage + bleeding gums + coiled hairs = scurvy (vitamin C deficiency).
also: Also swollen gums and poor wound healing

set_title: Skin signs of internal disease: Trousseau sign of malignancy, Leser-Trelat sign, Acanthosis nigricans, Necrolytic migratory erythema and Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
stem: A 63-year-old man has 3 months of weight loss, epigastric pain radiating to the back and jaundice. Over 2 weeks, tender cords of superficial thrombophlebitis have appeared in his left arm, then his right leg, then his chest wall.
oneliner: 63M, weight loss + jaundice + migratory tender superficial vein cords → ?

whyNot.A: Leser-Trelat is a sudden crop of keratoses; he has **tender venous cords**
whyNot.B: Acanthosis nigricans is velvety dark plaques; his lesions are **tender venous cords**
whyNot.C: Necrolytic migratory erythema is a blistering rash; his findings are **venous thromboses**
whyNot.E: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy causes clubbing and bone pain, not **migrating venous clots**

why: **Migratory superficial thrombophlebitis** with a pancreatic-type tumor is Trousseau sign of malignancy, from mucin-driven hypercoagulability.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Sudden eruption of many seborrheic keratoses
Velvety dark plaques in neck, axillae
Insulin resistance; abrupt onset: gastric adenocarcinoma
Spreading red blistering rash, groin, face
Clubbing with painful periostitis of long bones

idea.rule: Migratory thrombophlebitis + visceral cancer = Trousseau sign of malignancy.
also: Distinct from Trousseau sign of hypocalcemia

set_title: Bone imaging signs: Codman triangle, Sunburst pattern, Onion skin periosteum, Soap bubble lesion, Punched-out lytic lesions and Hair-on-end skull
stem: A 69-year-old man has 3 months of low back pain, fatigue and constipation. Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, calcium 12.4 mg/dL and creatinine 2.1 mg/dL; total protein is high and albumin low. A skull radiograph shows numerous sharply defined round lytic holes without surrounding sclerosis.
oneliner: 69M, back pain + anemia + hypercalcemia + renal injury + round lytic skull holes → ?
ask: Which diagnosis best explains this finding?

whyNot.A: Paget disease is sclerotic and thick; here are **round lytic holes with anemia**
whyNot.C: Osteosarcoma is a sclerotic metaphyseal tumor of adolescents, not **multiple lytic skull holes**
whyNot.D: Langerhans histiocytosis causes skull lesions in children, not **hypercalcemia at 69**
whyNot.E: Fibrous dysplasia gives ground-glass expansion, not **multiple lytic holes with anemia**

why: Punched-out lytic skull lesions with **hypercalcemia, anemia and renal impairment** indicate multiple myeloma: plasma cells activate osteoclasts without an osteoblast response.

idea.rule: Punched-out lytic lesions + CRAB features = multiple myeloma.
